open_points.subject: list_records record-type taxonomy
open_points.text: “a table keyed by the record type and total over its members” / `LISTABLE_RECORD_TYPES`
open_points.question: What closed record-type key set is this table total over, and how do its keys correspond to the MCP names such as `slots`, `contract versions` and `node executions`, given that no such enumeration or mapping is defined in `models`?
options: All persistent record types, with a boolean saying whether each is listable
Only the listable record types form the closed key set
A separate wire-name enumeration maps to model record classes
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed enumeration of the MCP-listable record types and map each member to its model record class.

open_points.subject: ownership of the list_records catalogue
open_points.text: “this module holds only the values” and “the refusal of an unlisted type or field `surface`'s” contradict “`surface`, which owns the catalogue”
open_points.question: Does `data_provider` own the allowed record-type/filter catalogue as policy data while `surface` only enforces it, or does `surface` own the catalogue itself?
options: `data_provider` owns the catalogue values and `surface` enforces them
`surface` owns and defines the catalogue
The catalogue is duplicated in both modules
open_points.default_guess: Treat `data_provider` as the sole owner of the catalogue values and `surface` as their enforcing consumer.

open_points.subject: StoreRepository page-row operation
open_points.text: “for a listed record type, its rows in store order, all of them or those whose column for one filter field equals a value”
open_points.question: What exactly does the new typed repository operation accept and return, especially for State 5's `field in a non-empty set` filter: does it accept a set, does `store` issue several equality reads and merge them, or does the repository return all rows for `store` to filter?
options: Repository accepts equality and set filters directly
Repository accepts one equality value and `store` performs and merges multiple reads
Repository returns all rows and `store` performs all filtering
open_points.default_guess: Let the repository accept the canonical equality-or-set filter and return matching rows in store order, leaving only page cutting to `store`.

open_points.subject: spool ceiling enforcement
open_points.text: “`store_spool` ... [owns] the two spool ceilings of A20, checked on publishing” contradicts “`store.spool_file` alone checks both ceilings of A15 rule 3” and `store.spool_file` saying it “Enforces ... `spool_file_bytes_max` ... and `spool_run_bytes_max`”
open_points.question: Which operation actually evaluates the two ceilings and decides the ceiling refusal: `store.spool_file` or `store_spool.publish_spool_entry`?
options: `store_spool` performs the checks and `store.spool_file` translates its result
`store` performs the checks and `store_spool` only publishes
Both check independently
open_points.default_guess: Have `store_spool` perform the checks and return a typed ceiling refusal that `store.spool_file` exposes.

open_points.subject: store_spool initialization and spool root
open_points.text: “The spool's on-disk layout below the spool area and the run directory” and “only `store` calls it”
open_points.question: How is `store_spool` given the spool-area root and initialized at `store.open_store`: is it constructed with the root once, does every call receive the root, or does it derive the root from hidden state not named by any operation?
options: `store` constructs a spool object once with the spool-area root
Every `store_spool` call receives the spool-area root
A module-global path is initialized by a missing setup operation
open_points.default_guess: Construct a spool object with the validated spool-area root during `store.open_store` and use that object for subsequent calls.

open_points.subject: store_spool.spool_entry_name
open_points.question: What are this operation's inputs and output, what validation or errors can it produce, and is its result an opaque bounded component or the actual relative filename?
options: SpooledFileKey in, one opaque relative component out, no failure for a valid key
Individual key fields in, relative path out, validation failures possible
The helper is private and is not callable by `store`
open_points.default_guess: Take a validated SpooledFileKey and return one opaque bounded relative component without I/O.

open_points.subject: store_spool.spool_attempt_prefix
open_points.question: What identifies an attempt for this operation, what does the returned prefix represent, and what injectivity/boundary guarantee lets discarding one attempt avoid matching another attempt's files?
options: Run, node, map index and attempt number in; an opaque exact-match prefix out
A complete SpooledFileKey in; prefix derived by dropping port and list index
The prefix operation is private and discard takes an attempt key directly
open_points.default_guess: Use an attempt key of run, node, optional map index and attempt number, with an encoding whose terminator prevents prefix collisions.

open_points.subject: store_spool layout hiding
open_points.text: The module “Hides ... the spool's on-disk layout ... [and] the temporary names” but publicly offers `spool_entry_name` and `spool_attempt_prefix`
open_points.question: Are the returned names opaque tokens that `store` must never interpret, are actual layout names intentionally exposed to `store`, or should these naming helpers be private to `store_spool`?
options: Make both naming helpers private
Return opaque tokens usable only in later `store_spool` calls
Expose actual relative names and remove the claim that layout is hidden
open_points.default_guess: Keep the naming helpers private and expose only key-based file operations.

open_points.subject: store_spool.publish_spool_entry
open_points.text: `publish_spool_entry` and “publishing one file complete, fsynced and digest-checked by a temporary and a rename, replacing a file at the same position”
open_points.question: What key, bytes, expected digest and expected size does publishing accept; what does it return; and how does it distinguish a ceiling refusal, digest/size mismatch, symbolic link, and other I/O failure for `store.spool_file`?
options: Accept key, bytes, expected digest and size; return facts or typed ceiling/integrity/I/O outcomes
Accept key and bytes; compute and return digest and size, with only ceiling and I/O outcomes
Accept an already-created temporary file and expected facts
open_points.default_guess: Accept the complete key, bytes and expected facts; return verified digest/size or typed ceiling, integrity, symlink and I/O outcomes.

open_points.subject: store_spool.publish_spool_entry attempt cleanup
open_points.text: “discarding every file of the refused attempt”
open_points.question: If publishing crosses a ceiling but removing an earlier file of that attempt fails or encounters a symbolic link, is the result still a ceiling refusal, an internal error, or a stop condition, and what files may remain and count afterward?
options: Return internal error unless the entire attempt was discarded
Return the ceiling refusal even if cleanup is incomplete and retry cleanup later
Make attempt publication atomic so partial cleanup cannot occur
open_points.default_guess: Return an internal error unless all files of the refused attempt were removed, while retaining any leftovers in subsequent ceiling accounting.

open_points.subject: store_spool.read_spool_entry
open_points.text: `read_spool_entry` and “reading a file back checked against a digest and size”
open_points.question: Does this operation receive a complete SpooledFileKey plus expected digest and size, what bytes or facts does it return, and how are a missing entry, digest/size mismatch, symbolic link and I/O failure reported to `store.read_value_bytes`?
options: Key and expected facts in; bytes or typed missing/integrity/symlink/I/O result out
Whole SpooledFile record in; bytes or one generic failure out
Key only in; module obtains expected facts from state despite owning no records
open_points.default_guess: Pass the key and expected digest/size and return bytes or a typed failure that `store` maps to `internal_error` for a recorded file.

open_points.subject: store_spool.discard_spool_attempt
open_points.question: What attempt identity does this operation take, is absence idempotent, does it remove final entries as well as temporaries, and what does it return when only part of the attempt can be removed?
options: Take an attempt key; idempotently remove all final and temporary entries; report any incomplete removal
Take the prefix returned by `spool_attempt_prefix`; remove final entries only
Take a complete entry key and infer the attempt
open_points.default_guess: Take the exact attempt key, idempotently remove all its final and temporary entries, and report incomplete removal as an I/O failure.

open_points.subject: store_spool.remove_spool_group
open_points.question: Is a spool group exactly a `run_id`; is removal idempotent for an absent directory; and what output and failure distinctions must `store.remove_run_spool` receive for partial removal, a symbolic link or another I/O error?
options: Group is `run_id`; absence succeeds; any incomplete removal is a typed I/O failure
Group is an opaque value produced elsewhere
Removal is best-effort and never reports failure
open_points.default_guess: Treat the group as `run_id`, make absence successful, and report symlink or incomplete removal as an I/O failure.

open_points.subject: store_spool.remove_spool_temporaries
open_points.text: `remove_spool_temporaries` and “removing the temporaries an interrupted publish left; refusing a symbolic link anywhere below the spool area”
open_points.question: Does this operation scan the whole spool area or one group, when exactly does `store.open_store` call it, what does it remove, and does any unreadable entry or symbolic link fail startup before anything is removed?
options: Scan the whole spool area during `open_store`; preflight links, then remove only recognized temporary files
Operate one run group at a time as groups are encountered
Remove recognized temporaries while scanning and fail when a later bad entry is encountered
open_points.default_guess: Scan the whole spool area during `open_store`, reject any symbolic link before mutation, then remove only names recognized as publish temporaries.
